name: Left ventricle
description: The thick-walled main pumping chamber. It sits in the middle of the parasternal views and on the right of the screen in apical views, and its size, wall thickness and contraction are the core of almost every echo report.

name: Right ventricle
description: The thinner-walled chamber that pumps blood to the lungs. It is the near-field chamber at the top of the parasternal long axis and sits on the left of the screen in the apical four chamber view, and enlargement or poor function points to right heart or pulmonary disease.

name: Left atrium
description: The chamber that receives blood from the pulmonary veins. It lies behind the aortic root in the parasternal long axis and at the bottom right of apical views. A large left atrium often reflects chronically raised filling pressure, mitral valve disease or atrial fibrillation.

name: Right atrium
description: The chamber that receives the venae cavae. It sits at the bottom left of the apical four chamber view and is entered by the IVC in subcostal views, and inward collapse of its wall is one of the echo signs that supports tamponade.

name: Aortic root
description: The first part of the aorta, including the sinuses of Valsalva that hold the aortic valve. It sits on the right of the parasternal long axis in front of the left atrium, where it is measured for dilation.

name: Ascending aorta
description: The tubular aorta above the sinotubular junction. It is seen beyond the root in a high parasternal long axis and on the left of the suprasternal view, and its dilation matters for aneurysm risk and aortic regurgitation.

name: Aortic valve
description: Three thin cusps between the LVOT and the aorta. They open against the aortic walls in systole and close to a central line in diastole, so thickening and poor opening point to aortic stenosis.

name: Right coronary cusp
description: The most anterior aortic cusp, giving rise to the right coronary artery. It is at the top of the valve in the parasternal short axis, next to the RVOT, and is the cusp nearest the transducer in the long axis.

name: Left coronary cusp
description: The cusp on the right side of the valve on screen in the parasternal short axis, toward the pulmonary artery. The left main coronary artery arises from its sinus.

name: Noncoronary cusp
description: The posterior cusp at the lower left of the valve in the parasternal short axis, next to the interatrial septum. No coronary artery arises from its sinus.

name: Mitral valve
description: The two-leaflet valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle. It opens widely in diastole and closes in systole, and it is checked for thickening, restricted opening, prolapse and vegetations.

name: Anterior mitral leaflet
description: The longer mitral leaflet, in fibrous continuity with the aortic root. In the parasternal long axis it swings toward the septum in early diastole, and in rheumatic stenosis it domes into a hockey stick shape.

name: Posterior mitral leaflet
description: The shorter mitral leaflet attached to the posterior annulus. In the parasternal long axis it lies next to the inferolateral wall, and it is often the leaflet that prolapses.

name: Tricuspid valve
description: The three-leaflet valve between the right atrium and the right ventricle. In the four chamber view it inserts slightly closer to the apex than the mitral valve, which helps tell the right heart from the left.

name: Pulmonic valve
description: The valve between the RVOT and the main pulmonary artery. It lies on the right of the screen in the parasternal short axis at the aortic valve level and is thin and often hard to see well in adults.

name: Main pulmonary artery
description: The arterial trunk beyond the pulmonic valve. In the short axis at the aortic level it runs toward the right of the screen and may show its bifurcation. A dilated trunk can be a sign of pulmonary hypertension.

name: Right ventricular outflow tract
description: The outflow part of the right ventricle leading to the pulmonic valve. In the short axis at the aortic level it wraps over the front of the aortic valve as the near-field structure.

name: Left ventricular outflow tract
description: The channel under the aortic valve, bounded by the septum and the anterior mitral leaflet. It is seen in the parasternal long axis and the apical five and three chamber views, and it narrows in systole in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

name: Interventricular septum
description: The muscular wall between the two ventricles. It crosses the top of the LV in parasternal views and runs vertically down the middle of the apical four chamber view, and its shape and thickness flag RV overload and hypertrophy.

name: Anterior wall
description: The LV wall facing the front of the chest, supplied by the left anterior descending artery. It is at the top of the LV in short axis views and on the right of the screen in the apical two chamber view.

name: Inferior wall
description: The LV wall resting on the diaphragm, usually supplied by the right coronary artery. It is at the bottom of the LV in short axis views and on the left of the screen in the apical two chamber view.

name: Anterolateral wall
description: The lateral LV wall. Its blood supply varies between people and comes from the circumflex artery, branches of the left anterior descending artery, or both. It is on the right of the screen in the apical four chamber and short axis views.

name: Inferolateral wall
description: The LV wall often called the posterior wall, usually supplied by the circumflex artery. It is the bottom wall of the LV in the parasternal long axis, where its thickness is measured, and on the left of the screen in the apical three chamber view.

name: Left ventricular apex
description: The tip of the LV, closest to the transducer at the top of apical views. Thrombus and takotsubo ballooning show here, and a foreshortened view hides it.

name: Interatrial septum
description: The thin wall between the two atria. It is seen best in subcostal views where the beam crosses it at a right angle, because apical views can show false dropout in its thin middle part.

name: Anterolateral papillary muscle
description: The papillary muscle on the right of the LV at about 3 to 4 o'clock in the short axis. It usually has a dual blood supply, which makes it less prone to ischemic rupture than the posteromedial muscle.

name: Posteromedial papillary muscle
description: The papillary muscle on the lower left of the LV at about 7 to 8 o'clock in the short axis. It usually depends on a single artery, which makes it the one more likely to rupture after infarction.

name: Moderator band
description: A muscular band crossing the apical third of the RV from the septum to the free wall, seen in the apical four chamber view. It identifies the chamber as the RV and is not a mass or thrombus.

name: Pericardium
description: The fibrous sac around the heart, seen as the brightest line behind the LV and left atrium in the parasternal long axis. Fluid between it and the heart is a pericardial effusion.

name: Pericardial space
description: The potential space between the visceral and parietal pericardium, normally no more than a thin dark line. It fills with fluid in an effusion, while a dark space seen only in front of the RV is often fat.

name: Coronary sinus
description: The vein that drains the heart into the right atrium along the posterior atrioventricular groove. It is a small round space behind the mitral annulus in the long axis, may be seen entering the right atrium in the RV inflow view, and lies in the atrioventricular groove in the apical two chamber view. Causes of a dilated sinus include a persistent left superior vena cava and raised right atrial pressure.

name: Eustachian valve
description: A normal remnant flap at the junction of the IVC and the right atrium. It is seen in the RV inflow and subcostal views and can be mistaken for a mass or thrombus.

name: Inferior vena cava
description: The large vein entering the right atrium from below. It runs through the liver in the subcostal IVC view, and its size and collapse with breathing estimate right atrial pressure.

name: Hepatic vein
description: A vein draining the liver into the IVC just below the right atrium. Seeing it join the vessel confirms you are looking at the IVC and not the aorta.

name: Liver
description: The near-field organ at the top of subcostal views. It is the acoustic window through which the beam reaches the heart and the IVC.

name: Diaphragm
description: The bright curved line between the liver and the heart in subcostal views. It separates the abdomen from the chest.

name: Descending thoracic aorta
description: The aorta running down behind the heart. It is a round circle behind the left atrium in the parasternal long axis and on the right of the suprasternal view, and it is the landmark that separates pericardial from pleural fluid.

name: Aortic arch
description: The curved segment of the aorta that gives off the head and neck vessels. It forms the top of the suprasternal view and is checked for dilation, coarctation and dissection.

name: Brachiocephalic artery
description: The first branch of the aortic arch. It rises from the top of the arch on the left side of the suprasternal image.

name: Left common carotid artery
description: The second branch of the aortic arch. It rises from the top of the arch between the other two branches in the suprasternal view.

name: Left subclavian artery
description: The third branch of the aortic arch. It rises from the top of the arch on the right side of the suprasternal image, just before the descending aorta. Coarctation usually sits just beyond its origin.

name: Right pulmonary artery
description: The branch pulmonary artery passing under the aortic arch. It appears as a round cross-section beneath the arch in the suprasternal view and confirms the plane.

name: Left atrial appendage
description: A small finger-like pouch off the left atrium, sometimes seen on the right side of the sector in the apical two chamber view. It is the usual site of clot in atrial fibrillation, but transthoracic echo often cannot show it well.
